Benefits of the Proposed Project
General Mitchell Field represents a substantial contribution to the Milwaukee Metropolitan economy. This can be measured in terms of direct employment and payroll, airline and airport services, and passenger contributions to the local economy. These expenditures create additional jobs, services and income. This demand for goods and services creates jobs and payrolls that might otherwise not exist in the area's economy. Additional benefits derived from General Mitchell Field are the business developments established along the edge of the airport facilities. These firms, dependent upon air travel or air cargo facilities, are restaurants, motels, and taxicab and limousine service companies, entertainment and exposition centers.
The airport itself is self-sustaining economically, producing about a 5% return on Milwaukee County's depreciated capital investment.
Milwaukee County is moving ahead with the implementation of its new Air Cargo Area and expanded air terminal facilities with large capital investments to better service area businesses and industries. These expanded facilities must be balanced with safe, efficient ground access.
This proposed project would benefit the local businesses by providing traffic relief to the existing street system in the vicinity of the airport. The projected vehicular traffic using Howell Avenue in 1990 is 16,300 vehicles per day north of the airport entrance road and 17,100 vehicles per day on the south. The vehicular traffic utilizing the air terminal facilities in 1990 is expected to be 29,250 vehicles per day. Of this projected traffic, 67% or 19,600 vehiles will be diverted to the proposed freeway facility.
